title: Mapo Tofu
subtitle: Sichuan silken tofu with pork and doubanjiang in a numbing chilli sauce
excerpt: Mapo tofu is one of the most famous Sichuan dishes: soft silken tofu in a fiery, numbing sauce made from doubanjiang (fermented chilli bean paste), Sichuan pepper, and pork mince. The characteristic mala (numbing and spicy) flavour comes from the combination of doubanjiang and Sichuan pepper.
sourceNotes: Mapo tofu originates from Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan province. The name translates roughly as 'pockmarked elderly woman's tofu', after the woman said to have created the dish in the late Qing dynasty. It is one of the defining preparations of Sichuan cooking and appears on menus worldwide.

content.text: Use silken tofu rather than firm tofu: the soft, quivering texture is essential. Add it carefully at the end and do not stir vigorously or the cubes will break. The cornflour slurry thickens the sauce so it clings to the tofu rather than pooling in the bowl. Doubanjiang is the heart of the dish: look for Pixian doubanjiang, which is more complex and fragrant than other brands.

Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil. Gently lower in the tofu cubes and simmer for 2 minutes to firm them slightly. Drain carefully and set aside. This step prevents the tofu from falling apart in the wok.

Heat the sunflower oil in the wok over high heat. Add the pork mince and fry, breaking it up, until browned, about 4 minutes. Add the doubanjiang and fry for 2 minutes until the oil turns red and the paste is fragrant.

Add the garlic and ginger and fry for 1 minute. Pour in 300 ml of water and the dark soy sauce. Bring to a simmer. Gently slide in the tofu cubes. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the wok gently (not stirring) to coat the tofu.
Pour in the cornflour slurry in a thin stream, stirring gently, until the sauce thickens. Add the chilli oil and Sichuan pepper. Serve in bowls over steamed rice, scattered with spring onion.

items.symptom: Tofu has broken into small pieces
items.cause: Tofu was stirred too vigorously, or a metal spatula was used
items.fix: Shake the wok gently or use a soft spoon to move the tofu. The par-boiling step at the start also helps firm it slightly.

items.symptom: Sauce is watery and does not cling to the tofu
items.cause: Not enough cornflour slurry, or slurry added all at once rather than gradually
items.fix: Add the slurry in stages, letting each addition thicken before adding more. The sauce should coat a spoon.
